models.claim: The model uses SI base units, the CODATA 2022 measured value of G, exact IAU nominal conversion constants where declared, and explicitly labelled conventional measured mass/radius estimates elsewhere.
models.validity: G is measured and uncertain; the astronomical unit and nominal solar radius are exact definitions. Kilogram mass estimates and mean planetary radii are not IAU nominal constants.

models.claim: Bound elliptic two-body states solve Kepler's equation and transform PQW state vectors into the inertial frame.
models.equation: M = E - e sin(E); r = a(1 - e cos(E))
models.validity: Osculating two-body ellipse with 0 <= e < 1; no parabolic or hyperbolic branch.

models.claim: Orbital-plane vectors use the active rotation Rz(Omega) Rx(i) Rz(omega) and an orthonormal sky basis.
models.validity: Right-handed Euclidean inertial coordinates; observer direction must be finite and non-zero.

models.claim: Planet and moon positions split their relative vector about the pair barycentre in inverse proportion to mass.
models.equation: r_p = r_b - m_m r_rel/(m_p+m_m); r_m = r_b + m_p r_rel/(m_p+m_m)
models.validity: Finite positive masses; missing masses deliberately disable the split in the educational compatibility path.

models.claim: Hill radius and empirical prograde/retrograde satellite limits are plausibility diagnostics, not stability proofs.
models.validity: Hierarchical restricted elliptic three-body diagnostic. The cited fit sampled planet/star mass ratio 10^-3, 0 <= e_p <= 0.9 and 0 <= e_s <= 0.5. Runtime fit messages allow only a 5% rounding band around that sampled mass ratio and emit HILL_FIT_OUT_OF_DOMAIN otherwise; do not interpret the fit as a proof for arbitrary masses, inclinations, resonances, or integration times.

models.claim: Exomoon TTV/TDV diagnostics derive from projected planet-moon barycentric motion and contact geometry.
models.equation: TTV = t_mid - (t_ref + N P); TDV = T_14/T_14,ref
models.validity: Synthetic event-series diagnostic; phenomenological orientation drifts are educational unless produced by integrated dynamics.

models.claim: Opaque circular and mixed-shape transits integrate the union of occulted stellar intensity without double counting overlaps.
models.equation: F = integral I(x,y) V(x,y) dA / integral I(x,y) dA
models.validity: Distant-observer projected geometry; grid tolerances must resolve the smallest structure. Current midpoint integrations do not return an a-posteriori error estimate and therefore are not research-validated.

models.claim: Quadratic and Claret intensity laws are evaluated exactly for supplied coefficients.
models.validity: Research use requires externally sourced passband- and atmosphere-specific coefficients; hand-derived fallbacks are educational.

models.claim: Transmissive occulters multiply radial transmissions while retaining an opaque physical core.
models.equation: F = integral I product_i T_i(rho_i) dA / integral I dA
models.validity: Transmission profiles are inputs; the TypeScript exponential halo is not a radiative-transfer solution.

models.claim: The preview lane supplies Lambert/cosine phase weights and a one-pole thermal-lag surrogate.
models.validity: Phenomenological broadband teaching model; not a temperature-map, energy-balance, or atmospheric emission solution.

models.claim: The preview forward-scattering lane evaluates an HG angular shape or a Gaussian phase surrogate.
models.validity: HG is a single-parameter angular approximation; current amplitude and finite-star geometry are not a research radiative-transfer model.

models.claim: Preview stellar flux, variability, spots, and granulation are bounded relative-flux teaching models.
models.equation: B_lambda(T)=2hc^2/[lambda^5(exp(hc/(lambda kT))-1)]; F_band proportional to R^2 integral B_lambda S(lambda) d lambda / integral S(lambda) d lambda
models.validity: Blackbody/surrogate filters, hand-derived limb coefficients, harmonic variability, and sinusoidal granulation are not atmosphere or PSD synthesis.

models.claim: Exposure smearing averages physical flux before seeded detector/observer perturbations are applied.
models.equation: F_exp(t) = Delta t^-1 integral F(tau) d tau
models.units: relative flux or electrons as explicitly configured
models.validity: Preview systematics are synthetic and mutable-state order dependent; they are not calibrated mission pipelines.

models.claim: Preview radial velocity is the barycentric target velocity projected with positive recession, while preview astrometry is a linear sky-plane displacement.
models.equation: v_r = -v dot n; r_sky = r-(r dot n)n
models.units: radial velocity [m s^-1], linear sky offset [m]
models.validity: The observer vector points from system to observer. V4 astrometry is not angular and has no distance/parallax calibration. The V5 backend requires an explicit RV target and projects photocentre offsets onto the sky plane.

models.claim: V4 constructs independently parameterized Kepler snapshots and composes a deterministic preview flux bundle.
models.validity: V4 executes independently parameterized Kepler snapshots only and must not label unavailable solvers as capabilities.

models.claim: V5 exposes a strict local contract and advertises error-controlled, provenance-complete Newtonian radial-velocity execution only when the pinned DOP853 dense representation and Arrow IPC are available.
models.equation: d^2 r_i/dt^2 = G sum_(j != i) m_j (r_j-r_i)/|r_j-r_i|^3; v_r = -v_target dot n
models.units: Cartesian state SI; epoch [JD TDB]; radial velocity [m s^-1]
models.validity: Barycentric, non-colliding Newtonian point masses with explicit target, numeric JD TDB epoch, finite radii, split absolute tolerances, and recorded provenance. Accepted dense numerical trajectories are certified outside finite-radius contact with bounded interval arithmetic; unsupported representations and unresolved bounds fail closed. Relativity, photometry, timing, atmosphere, astrometry artifacts, and inference are unavailable.
